accent.purpose: Actions, moving geometry, actual route, focus and contact results; headings stay graphite. rust is a legacy identifier.

paper.purpose: Page and field surface; reverse text on solid actions.

ink.purpose: Primary text, dark actions and selected controls.

line.purpose: Decorative dividers; not a control boundary.

control.purpose: Field and plan boundaries; planned route.

soft.purpose: Control groups, hover fills and reached-goal cells.

type-small.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-base.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-1.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-2.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-3.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-4.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-5.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-6.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-7.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

type-8.purpose: Built size step; the complete ramp advances by 1.25 with 1.5 leading.

display.purpose: Bold monochrome opening; type-9 at 1440px+, type-8 small desktop, type-7 tablet, type-5 phone.

headline.purpose: Bold monochrome workbench heading; type-6 desktop, type-5 tablet, type-4 phone.

title.purpose: Default h3; inspector and comparison titles override the size with type-1.

label.purpose: Secondary metadata; standard field labels remain body size.

measurement.purpose: Comparison measurement paragraphs; outputs, dd and table values use context-specific scale steps.

depth.interface: No CSS box-shadow or text-shadow tokens; separation uses tone, rules and spacing.
depth.scene: Orthographic Three.js geometry, PCF shadows and physical lighting. Imported models retain their own materials.

motion.name: control-color-change
motion.purpose: Actual base button transitions; timing function is implicit CSS ease.

motion.name: disclosure-arrow
motion.purpose: Last summary SVG rotates 90deg when details is open.

reducedMotion.behavior: CSS transition-duration becomes 0s, animation becomes none and scroll-behavior becomes auto. Playback starts paused; explicit replay remains available.

methodology.desktopColumns: 6 / 6 with one gutter, no empty track
methodology.headingSteps: type-8 wide desktop, type-7 small desktop, type-5 tablet, type-4 phone

importEntry.focus: panel summary on open, model review after reading, editor after acceptance

mobileContext.purpose: Live read-only plan with computed whole-run outcome and play/pause within the inspector.

interactionLimits.comparison: inputChanges reports effective settings and summarized route changes, including visual height. It is not a coordinate-level diff or proof of causal isolation.
interactionLimits.restore: Restores pinned experiment and replay speed/phase; undo recovers previous geometry. Visual files need reattachment.
interactionLimits.nearestContrast: Reached versus not-reached on the finite sampled grid. Manhattan index distance from nearest baseline-speed sample and phase index zero; ties prefer lower delay, then lower speed. Not an optimum or safe operating recommendation.

limitations: Source documentation only; no browser, rebuild or new review score. Final corrections are reviewed separately.
No synthetic eight-step tonalRamp is supplied because the implementation has no such scale.
Panel HTML/CSS demonstrates source styling, with root-variable fallbacks; static snippets do not implement React interactions or simulation.
Panel fonts inherit local app variables; without that environment the named family may fall back. Font files and licenses are recorded above.
Comparison remains two columns on phone; this is an implementation limit, not a required pattern for future screens.
Product-brief font sourcing and PALETTE.rust naming drift are documented, not repaired.

narrative.overview:
SceneBreaker presents editable geometry as a precise product study on cool porcelain. Graphite supplies structure; ultramarine draws attention to actions, movement and contact. Bold monochrome Familjen Grotesk headings replace the serif and coloured-italic treatment rejected by the user on October 8.

The same world continues into practical controls: readable sans-serif labels, monospaced measurements, restrained corners and explicitly named outcomes. The visual centerpiece is working Three.js geometry and an SVG plan, with motion started by the visitor. There is no authored raster artwork in this world; imported floorplans and models are user content.
keyCharacteristics: Three color anchors with derived opacity tones.
Familjen Grotesk bold monochrome headings and interface, Azeret Mono measurements.
Shared 12/8/4-track alignment and flat, ruled control groups.
Live spatial context and measured input-to-outcome comparisons.

rules.name: The Three Anchors Rule
rules.body: Derive interface tones from paper, ink and accent; keep user-imported imagery and model materials outside the interface palette.

rules.name: The Outcome Has a Name Rule
rules.body: Pair color with outcome text, geometry, line style or an icon; never make color the sole explanation of a result.

rules.name: The Whole Steps Rule
rules.body: Use the existing 1.25 scale and 1.5 line height; responsive type changes move between whole scale steps.

rules.name: The Flat Interface Rule
rules.body: Separate controls with tone, spacing and rules; let rendered scene geometry carry physical depth.

rules.name: The Compare Inputs Rule
rules.body: Explain a changed result with recorded effective inputs and replayable conditions; retain the finite-grid limits beside the finding.

dos: Do use the three anchors and their existing opacity-derived tones.
Do keep the exact 1.25 type steps, 150% leading and 12/8/4-track breakpoints.
Do load the two current font families locally and retain all bundled license files.
Do pair measured outcomes with text and show effective input differences beside comparisons.
Do preserve visible focus, accessible names, numeric validation and mobile spatial context.
donts: Don't restore the archived cream, forest and rust palette or Uncut/Spline typography.
Don't present a nearest sampled contrast as an optimum, safety score or exhaustive result.
Don't invent card, chip, shadow or motion primitives absent from the build.
Don't substitute decorative raster artwork for the live route study.
Don't treat this documentation pass, prior screenshots or target review scores as a fresh accessibility or quality certification.
